messages:
marisol_support: FYI, enterprise customer (AcmeCorp) opened an escalation — embedding endpoint behaving weirdly. They POST to /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-lite expecting 768-d vectors but we're returning 1536. Also, when they enable client-side batching (batch_size=8) their per-request latency jumps and tail latency spikes. Can someone help triage?

aaron_dev: thanks. can you paste the exact request payload + headers and a sample response? also need the model id they used (maybe alias mismatch).

marisol_support: pasted minimal repro below. sending trace id from their request headers: trace_id=trc-01G5XK4M

```json
{"model":"redwood-embed-lite","input":["query text..."],"batch_size":1}
```

response snippet: `{"data":[{"embedding":[/* length 1536 numbers */]}]}`

aaron_dev: hmm. two immediate possibilities: 1) the client requested a different model variant (e.g., -v2 which is 1536), or 2) we served a fused/quantized artifact with doubled dims due to preprocessing. can you confirm the model hash from the call (x-model-hash header) and the customer’s UI config?

marisol_support: they forwarded headers: `Authorization: Bearer sk-***`, `x-model-id: redwood-embed-lite`, `x-model-hash: d1f9a3c`

henry_sre: pinging infra. i'll pull the trace for trc-01G5XK4M and check routing. also note: batch scheduling can increase queue time — check the batch scheduler histogram + batch size distribution for that route.

tracing-bot: captured trace trc-01G5XK4M: route=\"embeddings.v1\" -> backend-node=embed-prod-7 -> kernel=quant-opt-v2. Spans: request.receive (2ms) -> router.queue (48ms) -> batch.exec (430ms) -> postprocess.kv (12ms).

julia_ml: that kernel name (quant-opt-v2) suggests we served a 1536-d quantized variant. If their client expected 768, either the alias binding is wrong in model catalog or our routing fallback picked a compatible model with different embedding size. check model catalog entry for redwood-embed-lite and the \"compatible_variants\" list.

marisol_support: customer insists they clicked the default model in console; they included UI screenshot showing \"redwood-embed-lite\" only. they also attached a short snip of logs showing repeated 429s when they try large batch sizes.

aaron_dev: can we repro internally? steps: 1) curl POST /v1/embeddings with x-catalog-env=prod and x-model-id=redwood-embed-lite, 2) try batch_size=8 and batch_size=1, 3) capture X-Serving-Model header and x-request-id. example curl:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY\" \
  -H \"x-model-id: redwood-embed-lite\" \
  -H \"x-catalog-env: prod\" \
  -d '{"input":["a","b","c"],"batch_size":8}'
```

henry_sre: i pulled the serving metadata for embed-prod-7: model bound=redwood-embed-lite@v2 (dim=1536), fallback policy allowed v2 for compatibility. That's the cause. But why would console show only \"redwood-embed-lite\"? dash-ops, do we show variant dropdown?

dash-ops: console hides variant by default; we show \"recommended\" in the UI but backend may route to v2 if it's marked compatible. we should add a conspicuous note for embedding dimension on the model card. filed ticket INF-8942.

julia_ml: for the latency/batching spike: tracing shows batch.exec=430ms — that's high. check the batch size distribution metric: metrics.embeddings.batch.size.p95. if they have small queueing tolerance, batch scheduler may wait to accumulate tokens which increases tail latency. Also check token-length distribution — longer prompts cause longer kernel time.

marisol_support: customer asked for per-request latency breakdown and where to find traces/dashboards to justify SLA credit. can we give them a link and a short explanation of relevant panels?

henry_sre: send them these dashboards: /dashboards/embeddings/per_request_breakdown (panels: request.receive, router.queue, batch.exec, kernel.time, postprocess.kv), /dashboards/embeddings/batch_histogram (panels: batch.size distribution, wait_time), and /dashboards/model-catalog/variant-bindings. For trace: point to Trace Explorer -> filter trace_id=trc-01G5XK4M. Provide a short CSV snippet they can use to correlate request IDs to billing records.

aaron_dev: mitigation steps for support to offer customer now: 1) pin model to explicit variant (e.g., redwood-embed-lite@v1) to guarantee 768-d outputs, 2) reduce client-side batch_size or switch to server-side auto-batching with latency SLO, 3) if they need throughput, recommend asynchronous job pattern with result pull and larger batch windows.

marisol_support: drafting reply to AcmeCorp with: explanation (we routed to v2 by compatibility), link to trace, link to dashboards, and recommended mitigations. will propose temporary SLA credit if we confirm routing misconfiguration. assigning follow-ups: INF-8942 (UI note), CUST-5234 (account pin request), and PROD-3257 (catalog binding audit).

julia_ml: also add an alert: if embedding output length mismatches expected dim for customer config, auto-surface an alert during onboarding. small UX win. :thumbsup:

marisol_support: thanks all — i'll update thread when customer acks.
